projects.purpose: Offline task planner with intelligent scheduling algorithm for students, optimizing study time and deadlines across multiple modes

memories.title: Project Identity and Core Purpose
memories.summary: Timely (codename Tasker) is a full-stack offline task/study planner combining PWA and Electron desktop app for intelligent task scheduling without internet dependency.
memories.content: The project targets students needing to manage complex study schedules with multiple subjects, deadlines, and exam preparation. Core philosophy: 'Full functional, 0 marketing. Sin rachas, logros ni gamificación. Solo herramientas que ayuden de verdad.' (No streaks, achievements, or gamification - only real tools). Exists as both PWA (progressive web app) installable via browser and Electron desktop application (Windows portable .exe). PWA deployed on Vercel, Electron built with electron-builder. Fully offline-capable with localStorage persistence (PWA) or JSON file database (Electron). Service Worker registered for complete offline functionality.

memories.title: Full-Stack Architecture: React + TypeScript + Vite + Electron
memories.summary: Frontend uses React 19 with TypeScript and Vite 5, state management via Context API + useReducer, with dual-backend support (Electron IPC + localStorage).
memories.content: Stack choices: React 19.2.1 for UI, TypeScript 5.3 for type safety, Vite 5.0 for fast bundling (base: './'), Electron 28 for desktop app, Vitest for testing. React components in src/components organized by feature (Calendar, Tasks, Common, Layout). Global state managed in src/app/store.tsx using createContext + useReducer pattern (no Redux). Two persistence layers: (1) PWA mode uses localStorage via api-mock.ts, (2) Electron uses IPC bridge to main process which manages JSON file database. Preload.ts secures contextIsolation=true, sandbox=true. All APIs abstracted through src/app/api.ts for environment-agnostic code.

memories.title: Directory Structure and Module Responsibilities
memories.summary: src/ splits into app/ (business logic), components/ (UI), pages/ (routes), styles/ (CSS); electron/ handles desktop main process and IPC.
memories.content: Structure breakdown: (1) src/app/ = core business logic: algo/scheduler.ts (1241 lines, multi-mode planning), api.ts (abstraction layer), store.tsx (state), types.ts (shared types), task-utils.ts (helpers), time.ts (date/time), api-mock.ts (localStorage backend). (2) src/components/ = UI: Calendar/ (BlockFormModal, ManualPlanModal, DayTasksModal, CompletePlanModal), Tasks/ (TaskFormModal, TaskDetailModal, TaskItem, TaskList), Common/ (Button, Modal, Icon, TaskTimer, StatCard), Layout/ (AppShell, Sidebar, Topbar, BottomNav). (3) src/pages/ = route pages: Today, Tasks, CalendarWeek, CalendarMonth, Settings, Help, LandingPage. (4) src/styles/ = global CSS. (5) electron/ = desktop: main.ts (app lifecycle, window creation), ipc.ts (inter-process handlers), preload.ts (secure API exposure), store/ (JSON database management). (6) public/ = static assets (icons, manifest, sw.js). Entry: src/main.tsx → React mount, App.tsx detects env (Electron/PWA/browser).

memories.title: Scheduler Algorithm: Multi-Mode Intelligent Planning
memories.summary: scheduler.ts implements X-Y-Z scoring with 8 planning modes (concentrado, equilibrado, variado, deadline_first, balanceo_asignaturas, progreso_uniforme, deadline_carga, tipo_tarea) considering urgency, priority, progress, momentum, and learning curve.
memories.content: Core algorithm in src/app/algo/scheduler.ts (1241 LOC) generates optimal task schedules. Key concepts: (1) TaskScore interface combines task, urgency, priority, risk_level (safe/warning/critical), momentum_bonus (continuity reward), learning_curve_factor (favor long sessions for new tasks). (2) Eight modes alter weighting: 'concentrado'=deep focus, 'equilibrado'=balanced, 'deadline_first'=prioritize by deadline, 'balanceo_asignaturas'=equalize subject time, 'progreso_uniforme'=proportional advancement, 'deadline_carga'=deadline+workload, 'tipo_tarea'=group by type. (3) Input: SchedulerInput (tasks, blocks, existingPlans, date, settings), output: SchedulerOutput (plans array + microplan). (4) Distributes planned hours across available time blocks respecting min_slice_h (0.5h min) and max_slices_per_task_per_day. (5) Settings.weights control X/Y/Z and w1-w5 factors (tunable per user preference). Status tracking: plans have status='planned'|'done'|'skipped'|'locked'.

memories.title: Data Model: Tasks, Blocks, Plans, Sessions
memories.summary: Task (title, type, priority, estimated_h, completed_h, deadline, status), Block (weekday, time, allowed types), Plan (task→date→block allocation), Session (time tracking) persist across runs.
memories.content: Core entities in src/app/types.ts: (1) Task: id, title, description, type ('Entrega'|'Examen'|'Extra'), priority (0-10 scale), estimated_h, completed_h, deadline (ISO string|null), status ('pending'|'in_progress'|'done'|'cancelled'), project_id, subject, timestamps. (2) Block: id, weekday (0-6), start_time/end_time (HH:MM), name, label, color, allowed ('Entregas'|'Exámenes'|'Extras'|'Todos'), requires_break, exclude_from_planner (for classes/fixed activities). (3) Plan: id, task_id, date (YYYY-MM-DD), start_time, end_time, slice_h (hours allocated), slice_index (which chunk of task), status, block_id. (4) Session: id, task_id, started_at/ended_at, minutes, notes. (5) Settings: theme, weights object (X,Y,Z,w1-w5), min_slice_h, max_slices_per_task_per_day, planner_mode, max_tasks_per_block, urgency_threshold_days. (6) Project, Tag, Subtask (not yet fully integrated). Current date stored in context as ISO string.

memories.title: State Management: Context + useReducer Pattern
memories.summary: AppProvider wraps app with global AppState (tasks, blocks, plans, projects, settings, currentDate, activeSession, loading, error); actions dispatched via useApp() hook.
memories.content: src/app/store.tsx defines AppState interface with 9 properties. reducer handles ~20 action types (SET_TASKS, ADD_TASK, UPDATE_TASK, DELETE_TASK, SET_BLOCKS, ADD_BLOCK, etc.). useApp() custom hook provides dispatch + read-only selectors. initialState loads currentDate as today's YYYY-MM-DD. Async data refresh happens via useEffect in App.tsx on mount, loading=true during fetch. No local component state for core data (lifted to context). Sessions and active session managed here for timer functionality.

memories.title: Persistence Layer: API Abstraction with Mock Backend
memories.summary: src/app/api.ts wraps window.api (Electron) vs apiMock (PWA localStorage), exposing: settings, tasks, blocks, plans, sessions, projects endpoints with typed CRUD.
memories.content: api.ts maintains isElectron flag (currently hardcoded false for PWA testing). Each resource (settings, tasks, blocks, plans, sessions, projects) has methods: get/list, create, update, delete, byId. apiMock.ts uses localStorage with STORAGE_KEYS (tasker_tasks, tasker_blocks, etc.). Default settings include theme='light', min_slice_h=0.5, planner_mode='equilibrado'. Electron version in electron/ipc.ts delegates to jsondb.ts which reads/writes JSON file. Result<T> wrapper ensures consistent error handling (ok: true/false + data|error). All API calls are async. Preload validates window.api exists before exposure.

memories.title: UI Organization: Page-Driven Navigation with Modal Patterns
memories.summary: App.tsx route-switches between 6 pages (Today, Tasks, CalendarWeek, CalendarMonth, Settings, Help); AppShell wraps layout (Topbar, Sidebar, BottomNav); modals handle detail views.
memories.content: Pages in src/pages/: (1) Today = daily quick view with today's plans, blocks, timer, recalculation button; shows task warnings (alerts for critical/warning tasks). (2) Tasks = filterable task list with pagination, create/edit/delete, detail view. (3) CalendarWeek = grid (weekday × hour 6:00-24:00) showing blocks and ability to manually assign tasks. (4) CalendarMonth = monthly view of deadlines and plan distribution. (5) Settings = planner mode selector, weight tuning (X/Y/Z/w1-w5), theme toggle. (6) Help = documentation. LandingPage shown only if not installed (no Electron + not PWA). AppShell (Layout/AppShell.tsx) renders Topbar + [Sidebar (desktop) | BottomNav (mobile)] + page content. Modal patterns: TaskFormModal (create/edit), TaskDetailModal (read), BlockFormModal (blocks), ManualPlanModal (assign task to block), CompletePlanModal (log actual time).

memories.title: Dual Deployment: Vercel (PWA) + Electron Desktop
memories.summary: vercel.json configures PWA deployment with Service Worker caching strategy; electron-builder.json packages Windows portable .exe with electron-builder --config --win portable.
memories.content: PWA deployment: Vercel rewrite rule (.*) → /index.html (SPA support). Service Worker (sw.js) cached with max-age=0 (always check for updates), manifest.json cached 24h, other assets aggressively cached. Security headers: nosniff, X-Frame-Options=DENY, XSS-Protection=1. npm scripts: 'dev' runs Vite + Electron concurrently, 'build' = Vite build, 'build:electron' = tsc on tsconfig.electron.json, 'build:desktop' = npm run build && run build:electron && electron-builder. Electron: main process loads index.html from dist/electron/main.js, dev mode loads http://localhost:5173, production loads bundled file. electron-builder targets Windows portable (x64). Preload.ts uses contextIsolation to securely expose API. Both targets support full offline work.

memories.title: Known Issues and Future Improvements from IDEAS.md
memories.summary: Critical and Warning alert system not functioning properly; algorithm recommendation logic needs tuning (e.g., recommending month-ahead task over week-near task of similar effort); Help documentation outdated after subtask time removal.
memories.content: From IDEAS.md end notes: (1) 'Críticos y Advertencia no funcionan bien' - severity alerts should appear as side panel alerts, not count full weeks, only same week. (2) Algorithm can recommend suboptimally (e.g., Prio3 task due in 30 days vs Prio3 task due in 7 days with similar workload - should prefer the urgent one). (3) 'Help no está actualizado tras quitar el tiempo de subtareas' - Help page references removed subtask time feature. (4) Test suite exists (scheduler.spec.ts, scripts/test-*.ts) but needs comprehensive validation across all 8 modes with diverse task sets. (5) Proposed future modes: 'Deep Work' (long 2-4h sessions), 'Quick Wins' (<1h tasks), 'Deadline + Carga' hybrid logic needs refinement. (6) No task dependencies yet, no calendar integration (Google/Outlook), no estimation learning from history, no collaborative mode.

projects.purpose: Distributed systems coursework: multi-client TCP chat, broker-based FileManager with service discovery, load balancing, keep-alive mechanisms, containerization with Docker, and Kubernetes orchestration.

memories.title: Project Structure & Evolution
memories.summary: Six major deliverables progressing from basic TCP chat (Entrega1-2) through distributed FileManager with broker (P1fileManager) to containerized Kubernetes deployment (P2FileManager), plus Lambda serverless computing for calculator with RDS.
memories.content:
Entrega1-2: TCP chat client-server with multi-threading, public/private messaging, user listing. Entrega2 included Chat-specific memory documentation.

P1fileManager: FileManager distributed system with 3-tier architecture (Broker-Server-Client), introduction of RPC pattern, service discovery, keep-alive/heartbeat.

P2FileManager: Production deployment with Docker (broker-build, server-build Dockerfiles) and 3 Kubernetes scenarios (basic, advanced-hostpath, advanced-nfs).

Tutorial2_Database: Database instead of FileManager as service, demonstrating architecture reusability.

python/lambda-package: AWS Lambda functions for calculator operations (+, -) with RDS MySQL backend.

CHEATSHEETS_EXAMEN: Study guides for AWS (EC2, Lambda, RDS, Databases), Kubernetes/Dockerfile, and core distributed systems concepts.

memories.title: Broker-Mediated Service Architecture
memories.summary: Three-tier system: Broker (port 1066) mediates service discovery and load balancing; multiple Servers (port 1067) register and maintain heartbeat; Clients query broker for least-loaded server, then connect directly to assigned server for persistent session.
memories.content:
BROKER: Listens on port 1066, maintains map of registered servers with metadata (IP, port, numClients, keepAliveCounter, alive flag). Uses threads to handle ephemeral connections. Implements keep-alive monitoring every 5 seconds; after KEEP_ALIVE_MAX_COUNT (=2) missed signals, marks server as dead but doesn't delete.

SERVER: Registers via SERVER_CONNECT message (broker assigns connection ID). Launches background keep-alive thread sending ACK_BROKER every 5 seconds. Opens listening port (1067) for client connections. Maintains map of FileManager instances per client.

CLIENT: Queries broker via CLIENT_CONNECT to discover server. Broker responds with address of server with least clients (round-robin by load). Client connects to assigned server persistently. Connection closes only after destructorFilemanager.

Key insight: Broker connections are EPHEMERAL (open-send-close), server-client connections are PERSISTENT. This reduces resource overhead on broker.

memories.title: Message Serialization & Protocol
memories.summary: Pack/unpack template functions in utils.h serialize C++ types to byte buffers; every message starts with type enum, followed by parameters in fixed order; sendMSG/recvMSG wrap TCP with 4-byte size prefix.
memories.content:
Serialization (utils.h templates):
- pack<T>(buffer, value): Append type T to buffer
- unpack<T>(buffer): Extract next T from buffer (destructive)
- packv/unpackv: Handle arrays (string = size + chars)

Protocol layers:
1. Application: enum types (brokerMsgTypes: SERVER_CONNECT, CLIENT_CONNECT, ACK_BROKER; msgTypes: constructorFilemanager, listFilesF, readFileF, writeFileF, destructorFilemanager, ack)
2. Transport: sendMSG/recvMSG add 4-byte int size prefix before data, handle partial reads
3. Network: TCP sockets (socket, connect, bind, listen, accept, read, write, close)

Critical: pack/unpack order must match on both sides. Strings always transmit as (int_size, char_array).

memories.title: Multi-Threading Concurrency Model
memories.summary: One thread per connection (server listening spawns thread per accept, broker spawns thread per client message). Shared data structures (serversMutex protects servidoresRegistrados map) use lock_guard<mutex> for thread safety.
memories.content:
Broker: Infinite listen loop calls accept(), spawns thread for each connection running resolveBrokerMessages(). Each thread handles one message type (SERVER_CONNECT registers server, CLIENT_CONNECT finds least-loaded server).

Server: Main thread listens for clients, spawns thread per accepted connection. Each thread:
- Receives constructor message (instanciates FileManager)
- Loop: receives operation (listFiles, readFile, writeFile)
- Sends response
- Receives destructor, deletes instance, closes connection

Threadsafety: 
- serversMutex guards servidoresRegistrados (read/write by keep-alive monitor and request handlers)
- lock_guard<mutex> lock(serversMutex) ensures atomic section
- clientList and instanciasFileManager protected by platform-level concurrency

Detach vs join: Threads detach() to auto-cleanup; no explicit join().

memories.title: Keep-Alive / Heartbeat Mechanism
memories.summary: Server sends ACK_BROKER keep-alive to broker every 5 seconds; broker monitor thread increments keepAliveCounter for each server; if counter exceeds KEEP_ALIVE_MAX_COUNT (2), marks server alive=false to prevent new client assignment.
memories.content:
Keep-alive flow:
1. Server spawns background thread: while(alive) { every 5s: connect broker -> send ACK_BROKER + serverID -> close }
2. Broker monitor thread: every 5s: for each server { keepAliveCounter++ } ; if counter > 2: alive=false
3. On new CLIENT_CONNECT, broker only assigns servers with alive=true

Detection time: up to 15 seconds (KEEP_ALIVE_MAX_COUNT=2 * 5s heartbeat intervals) before dead server marked as unusable. However, broker does NOT delete entry, so server can recover if it reconnects.

Relevance: Essential for fault tolerance in distributed systems. Decouples failure detection from client-server communication.

memories.title: FileManager Distributed Implementation
memories.summary: Client-side FileManager (distributedFileManager.cpp) overloads constructor to query broker, connect to assigned server, and forward method calls as RPC messages; server-side FileManager instances instantiated per client and map to serialized responses.
memories.content:
Client-side (distributedFileManager.cpp):
- FileManager(): calls obtenerServidorDelBroker() (CLIENT_CONNECT -> broker queries -> assigns server -> stores assignedServerIp/Port static vars)
- FileManager(path): same + sends constructorFilemanagerParams to server
- listFiles(): packs listFilesF -> sendMSG -> recvMSG -> unpack vector<string>
- readFile(fileName, data): packs readFileF + fileName -> sendMSG -> recvMSG -> unpack data
- writeFile(fileName, data): packs writeFileF + fileName + data -> sendMSG -> recvMSG
- ~FileManager(): packs destructorFilemanager -> sendMSG -> recvMSG -> closeConnection

Server-side (clientManager.cpp):
- Maintains map<int, FileManager> instanciasFileManager (key = clientId)
- Receives messages, unpacks type, instantiates/calls/destroys FileManager, repacks response
- Static in distributedFileManager: map<FileManager*, int> connectionIds (for reverse lookup)

File paths: P1fileManager/fileManager/{distributedFileManager.cpp, clientManager.cpp, fileManager.h}

memories.title: Containerization & Kubernetes Deployment Strategies
memories.summary: Three progressively complex scenarios: basic (no volumes, stateless), advanced-hostpath (local node storage, pods share within node), advanced-nfs (shared NFS across all pods/nodes with PersistentVolume+PersistentVolumeClaim).
memories.content:
BASIC (k8s-files/basic):
- broker.yaml: Deployment (1 replica) + Service (NodePort 32002), image skitemplar/broker-filemanager:v1
- server.yaml: Deployment (2 replicas) + Service, with args passing BROKER_SERVICE_SERVICE_HOST from K8s DNS
- No volumes; each pod instance has independent FileManagerDir

ADVANCED-HOSTPATH (k8s-files/advanced-hostpath):
- server.yaml with volumeMounts: { mountPath: /FileManagerDir }
- volumes: { hostPath: { path: /srv/filemanager/hostpath } }
- Pods on same node share files; pods on different nodes do not

ADVANCED-NFS (k8s-files/advanced-nfs):

memories.title: Kubernetes YAML Structure & Key Concepts
memories.summary: All K8s YAMLs require apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec. Deployment selector.matchLabels must match template.metadata.labels. Service selector targets pods. ContainerPort ↔ targetPort must align. PV/PVC storageClassName must match.
memories.content:
Deployment template (apps/v1):
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name, namespace}
spec:
  replicas: N
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: label}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: label}}  # MUST match selector
    spec:
      containers:
      - name, image, ports: [{containerPort}], env, volumeMounts
      volumes: [{name, hostPath/persistentVolumeClaim/emptyDir}]
```

Service template (v1):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name}
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector: {app: label}  # MUST match Deployment labels
  ports: [{port, targetPort, nodePort, protocol}]
```

PersistentVolume (v1):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name}
spec:
  storageClassName: X
  capacity: {storage: 10Gi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteMany]
  nfs: {server: IP, path: /path}
```

PersistentVolumeClaim (v1): Similar structure, requests storage from PV with matching storageClassName.

projects.purpose: Trilogía histórica épica medieval (3 libros, ~1.165 páginas) sobre el nacimiento del Imperio de Castilla en el siglo X-XI, desde la fundación de un reino por Dánegan (931) hasta la muerte del último Mariscal (1035).

memories.title: Estructura narrativa de la saga completa
memories.summary: Trilogía de 3 libros (~1.165 páginas): Libro 1 'La Era de Dánegan' (931-968, ~365 pp), Libro 2 'Los Conquistadores' (968-1000, ~400 pp), Libro 3 'Los Últimos Grandes' (1000-1035, ~400 pp); eje narrativo = pregunta central 'puede un hombre construir algo que sobreviva a su muerte.'
memories.content: Cada libro tiene 7-12 capítulos + Prólogo + Epílogo. Libro 1 es la era de Dánegan I (protagonista), Libro 2 la era de sus herederos Juan I y Gonzalo I con los 11 Grandes construyendo imperio, Libro 3 es la cuenta atrás: los 11 mueren uno a uno (1017-1030) hasta que solo USER queda (muere 1035 a los 71 años). Sin magia, sin sobrenaturalismo, épica histórica medieval realista con multiplicador militar x1.5 sobre historia estricta.

memories.title: Los 11 Grandes como hermandad (no institución)
memories.summary: Los 11 personajes principales son amigos de infancia entrenados por García Dánegan desde ~975, seleccionados por Gonzalo I como hermandad en 984, renuncian a títulos individuales para gobernar juntos vía Gran Consejo.
memories.content: Exactamente 11, orden de muerte inmutable: Santiago (1017, 52), Alfonso (1018, 52), Juan (1020, 53), Targon (1022, 55), Kaven (1023, 58), Cerve (1024, 57), Alejandro (1025, 62), Aldo (1026, 63), Deon (1030, 66), Gonzalo (1030, 66), USER (1035, 71). Cada uno tiene rol diferenciado (USER=Mariscal, Alfonso=Canciller, etc.) y ranking fijo como guerreros y comandantes. La hermandad no es institución política sino lazos de sangre/crianza — luego se institucionaliza en el Gran Consejo bajo Gonzalo.

memories.title: Story Bible como fuente única de verdad
memories.summary: Directorio /story-bible contiene 6 archivos canónicos: master-plan.md (visión macro), characters.md (fichas psicológicas), timeline.md (cronología multinivel 905-1035), plot-arcs.md (arcos narrativos), rules.md (14 decisiones inamovibles DEC-001 a DEC-014), writing-roadmap.md (orden de escritura no-cronológico por pilares).
memories.content: Ubicación exacta: C:/Users/USER/PERSONAL/Libro/Libro/story-bible/. Antes de escribir cualquier escena TOLKIEN consulta estos archivos. Los 14 DEC definen lo inmutable: fechas de muerte de los 11 (DEC-001/DEC-014 compresión de 15 años), renombramiento Elvira/Jimena (DEC-002), nacimiento Blanca 934 (DEC-003), trilogía confirmada (DEC-004), nombre 'Imperio de Castilla' (DEC-005), alcance de conquista (DEC-006), estructura 11+8+7 capítulos (DEC-007), realismo militar x1.5 (DEC-008), etc.

memories.title: Skill TOLKIEN — el co-escritor permanente
memories.summary: Skill interactivo en /tolkien-skill/SKILL.md y /tolkien.skill que activa el 'modo Dánegan': escritor que consulta Story Bible antes de cada escena, verifica consistencia, detecta plot holes, escribe prosa medieval épica tercera persona omnisciente.
memories.content: TOLKIEN es el co-escritor de USER. No es asistente genérico sino guardián de la consistencia del universo. Workflow: 1) LEER timeline+characters para período, 2) VERIFICAR qué existe antes/después, 3) DETECTAR decisiones pendientes, 4) PREGUNTAR solo si crítico, 5) ESCRIBIR prosa editorial no borrador, 6) VERIFICAR consistencia contra rules.md, 7) SUGERIR actualizaciones Story Bible. Activa cuando USER dice 'Tolkien', 'modo escritor', 'escribe el libro', 'revisa el capítulo', etc.

memories.title: Geopolítica del imperio en apogeo (~1025)
memories.summary: En su máxima expansión el Imperio de Castilla controla: Iberia completa (Toledo 987, Barcelona 994, Cádiz 997), Gascuña + corredor pirenaico (1007), Aquitania/Languedoc/Provenza (1013), corredor norteafricano Ceuta-Tánger-Argel (1008-1012), sur de Inglaterra + SE Irlanda + Dinamarca norte (1032), vasallaje noruego (1001).
memories.content: NO conquista: París (invadida 1019 para dictar términos, no anexionada), Escocia/norte Inglaterra/norte Irlanda, Escandinavia más allá de Noruega meridional, interior de África (derrota Al-Wadi 1015 detiene expansión). Justificaciones logísticas obligatorias en cada batalla: Francia dividida + alianza Sacro Imperio + 3 generaciones superioridad militar; África costera = control naval Estrecho + alianzas locales; Inglaterra = flota superior + desgaste inglés post-guerra civil.

memories.title: Compresión temporal DEC-014 y expectativas de vida
memories.summary: Saga termina en 1035 (no 1050): todos eventos Libro 3 adelantados ~15 años para que los 11 mueran a edades realistas 52-71 años en lugar de 66-86; USER muere a los 71 en su cumpleaños (17 junio 1035) tras vivir la última batalla naval Rivergreen.
memories.content: DEC-014 es crítica porque hace creíble la mortalidad de guerreros medievales de alta clase sometidos a décadas de combate activo. Antes la compresión no existía (versiones pre-abril 2026 decían 1050 para USER). Ahora Santiago muere 1017/52, Juan 1020/53, etc. hasta USER 1035/71. Las edades reflejan expectativa de vida de aristocracia militar post-Edad Media, no longevidad novelística anacrística.

memories.title: Reglas narrativas inamovibles
memories.summary: Tercera persona omnisciente (voz medieval épica, no moderna); tono grave sin artificialidad; diálogos en español moderno con dignidad medieval; cero magia/milagros/sobrenaturalismo; fe cristiana como motivación real (confesión, unción, peregrinaje) no como fuerza mística.
memories.content: Dánegan y Gonzalo pelean en primera línea siempre; todos los 11 pelean en primera línea (es su sello narrativo). Las batallas tienen coste — nunca se ganan limpias, siempre hay pérdida nombrada. Los números importan pero táctica supera número consistentemente. Una batalla no dura más de un día en narración sin salto temporal justificado. Ranking guerrero/comandante (Alejandro #1 guerrero, USER #1 comandante) son referencias conductales, no de orgullo — nunca se jactan.

memories.title: Estado actual de escritura y roadmap no-cronológico
memories.summary: Escrito: Prólogo L1, Cap 1-2 L1, Cap 3 L1 (parcial: falta batalla Salamanca). Writing-roadmap.md define orden de escritura = primero 7 pilares narrativos (Prólogo L1, Cap 1-2, Cap 11 L1, Prólogo L2, Cap 14 L2, Cap 4 L2), luego 6 pivotes, luego 15 capítulos en grupos A-G paralelizables.
memories.content: Principio rector: NO escribir en orden cronológico. Escribir pilares primero (196 pp estimadas) fija voz/tono/destino; después pivotes (214 pp); después relleno (grupo A=batallas L1, B=familia L1, C=epílogo L1, D=fundación L2, E=guerras L2, F=bisagra L2, G=cumbre L2). Con pilares hechos (7 meses estimados) USER tiene espina dorsal y puede afrontar crisis creativa. Roadmap v2.0 consolida blueprints canónicos contra títulos actuales (previamente había desalineación entre roadmap v1.0 y carpeta chapter-blueprints/).

memories.title: Tema central: el precio de la grandeza colectiva
memories.summary: Libro 1 = deber vs deseo (Dánegan no quiso ser rey, grandeza del ejemplo). Libro 2 = hermandad como motor (11 amigos renuncian títulos para imperio). Libro 3 = amistad vs tiempo (tiempo gana siempre; los 11 mueren uno a uno; USER sobrevive no por ser el más grande sino por aceptar ser el último).
memories.content: Macro-tema: el Imperio de Castilla no fue obra de un hombre sino de soldado→rey + nieto→emperador + once amigos que prefirieron morir juntos antes que vivir separados. La respuesta a la pregunta central es sí, un hombre (Dánegan) construyó algo que sobrevive (el Imperio que en Libro 3 sigue bajo Gonzalo II hijo de Gonzalo). Pero el precio es invisible hasta L3: la amistad no puede ganarle al tiempo. USER muere solo en su cama llevando la armadura de Targon, y el imperio sigue. La grandeza existe pero la soledad es el costo real.

memories.title: Personajes secundarios de peso narrativo
memories.summary: Damián (traidor/cómplice, muere ~974), Munio (conspirador primero, muere 962), García Dánegan (tío mentor, muere 979), Fray Sebastián (confesor moral, muere ~985), Beltrán de las Médulas (POV soldado raso), Ibn Yusuf (médico emirato), Hassan al-Mansur (antagonista L2, muere 987), Felipe II Francia (antagonista L3, decapitado 1019), Edmund Wessex (antagonista Anglo-castellano), María de Nuremberg (esposa Gonzalo, alianza Sacro Imperio, muere 1028).
memories.content: Cada secundario tiene ficha en characters.md. Los antagonistas (Hassan, Felipe II, Edmund) están dimensionados en lugar de ser monolíticos: Hassan elige la guerra solo; Felipe II hereda rabia de su padre; Edmund es joven ambicioso, no malvado. Personajes religiosos (Fray Sebastián, Alejandro que reza en árabe nombres de muslimes asesinados) mantienen Fe cristiana como motivación real sin sentimentalismo. Beltrán y otros personajes rasos anclan la tragedia en lo humano — tienen familia en casa que los espera, mueren por deber no por gloria.
